title.purpose: Tab labels, button text, emphasised rows.

body.purpose: Running text, table cells, descriptions. Tajawal leads the stack.

label.purpose: Badges, captions, metadata. Error text drops to 11px at the same weight.

shadows.name: ambient-rest
shadows.purpose: Every card and panel at rest. Navy-tinted so it reads as light rather than dirt.

shadows.name: ambient-lift

shadows.name: selection-ring

shadows.name: pulse-glow
shadows.purpose: Attention pulse keyframe in Shallow Water Blue. Used sparingly on elements awaiting action.

motion.name: field-focus

components.css: .ds-card { background: #fff; border-radius: 16px; padding: 20px; box-shadow: 0 4px 20px rgba(27,46,94,0.08); transition: all 0.3s ease; } .ds-card:hover { box-shadow: 0 8px 32px rgba(27,46,94,0.18); transform: translateY(-2px); } .ds-card-title { margin: 0 0 6px; font-family: 'Inter', 'Tajawal', sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 17px; color: var(--primary, #1B2E5E); } .ds-card-body { margin: 0; font-family: 'Tajawal', 'Inter', sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.6; color: #3D5A80; }

components.name: Text Field
components.description: Leading-icon field. Border shifts to navy on focus with no ring or glow.
components.css: .ds-field { position: relative; } .ds-field-icon { position: absolute; top: 50%; transform: translateY(-50%); right: 12px; color: #7A9BB5; pointer-events: none; display: flex; } .ds-field-input { width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box; background: #fff; border: 1.5px solid var(--border, #D0DFF0); border-radius: 10px; padding: 11px 40px 11px 12px; font-family: 'Tajawal', 'Inter', sans-serif; font-size: 14px; color: var(--primary, #1B2E5E); outline: none; transition: border-color 0.2s; } .ds-field-input::placeholder { color: #7A9BB5; } .ds-field-input:focus { border-color: var(--primary, #1B2E5E); }

components.name: Week Tabs
components.description: Segmented navigation. Active fills navy; resting tabs carry a Tide Line border.
components.css: .ds-tabs { display: flex; gap: 8px; } .ds-tab { padding: 10px 24px; border-radius: 10px; font-family: 'Inter', 'Tajawal', sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 15px; cursor: pointer; transition: all 0.3s ease; border: 2px solid var(--border, #D0DFF0); background: #fff; color: #3D5A80; } .ds-tab:hover { border-color: var(--secondary, #7BB8D4); } .ds-tab:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--secondary, #7BB8D4); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-tab--active { background: var(--primary, #1B2E5E); color: #fff; border-color: var(--primary, #1B2E5E); }

components.name: Progress Bar

components.css: .ds-progress { height: 12px; background: var(--border, #D0DFF0); border-radius: 6px; overflow: hidden; } .ds-progress-fill { height: 100%; width: 68%; background: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--secondary, #7BB8D4), var(--primary, #1B2E5E)); border-radius: 6px; transition: width 1s ease; }

narrative.overview:
Prime Fit looks like a well-run clinic with a view of the water. It is composed and precise, because it asks people to upload blood tests and trusts them with guidance in return — but it is lit by Gulf daylight, not fluorescent tube. The whole palette is cool blues on a bright, slightly cool paper: deep navy for authority, sky and tide blues for everything the user can act on, and a pale sea-mist ground that keeps the interface feeling open rather than clinical.

Depth is atmosphere, not architecture. Surfaces float on soft, navy-tinted shadows the way paper sits on a desk in daylight — a shadow here means "this is a thing you can pick up," never "this ranks above that." Components are soft, calm and unhurried: generously rounded, nothing sharp, nothing shouting. Someone opens this between sets, one-handed, half-paying-attention, and nothing in the interface should raise their heart rate further.

Arabic is not a mode in this system — it is the ground state. direction: rtl is set on the html element itself, and English is the override. That single fact drives more layout decisions than any grid: every new surface is laid out in logical properties and read right-to-left first.

The one thing this system must never become is the other end of its own metaphor: a cold medical records screen. Grey-on-grey, borderless density, no daylight. The clinic half supplies precision; the Gulf half supplies the reason anyone would want to open it.
keyCharacteristics: Cool-blue spectrum only; warmth appears exclusively as semantic signal
RTL-first layout, with Inter and Tajawal both present in every font stack
Soft ambient shadows, navy-tinted, 2px hover lift
16px cards, full-pill badges, nothing with a sharp corner
Calm density — generous padding, no compressed tables

rules.name: The Cool Spectrum Rule
rules.body: Every structural colour is a cool blue between Deep Harbour Navy and Sea Mist. Warmth enters only as a semantic signal. A warm decorative accent — a gold border, an orange heading, a red that isn't an error — is outside the system.

rules.name: The Navy Text Rule
rules.body: Body text is Deep Harbour Navy, not black and not grey. Pure black on Sea Mist reads as a foreign element pasted into the page.

rules.name: The Two-Script Rule
rules.body: Every font stack lists both Inter and Tajawal, in the order appropriate to its role. A mixed Arabic/English string — which in this product is most strings — must never fall through to a system default mid-sentence.

rules.name: The Heavy-Head Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is carried by weight, not size. The jump from body to display is 14px to 20px but 400 to 800. Reaching for a larger size before a heavier weight produces the wrong system.

rules.name: The RTL-First Rule
rules.body: Arabic is the ground state and English is the override. New layout is reasoned about right-to-left first and written in logical properties. left and right in a style object are a defect unless they are being chosen from the language state.

rules.name: The Breathing Room Rule
rules.body: Density is never the answer to too much content. Padding below 12px inside a card, or gaps below 8px between controls, belongs to the cold-records failure mode this system rejects.

rules.name: The Daylight Rule
rules.body: Shadows are tinted with the navy (rgba(27,46,94,...)), never neutral black. A grey or black shadow on Sea Mist reads as dirt rather than light.

rules.name: The Lift-on-Touch Rule
rules.body: The 2px rise on hover is the system's one physical gesture. It belongs to things that can actually be picked up — cards, tappable rows. A static panel that lifts is lying about what it does.

rules.name: The Soft Corner Rule
rules.body: 16px for containers, 12px for controls, pill for badges. A 0px or 4px corner is outside the system, and a radius above 16px on a large surface starts reading as a toy.

rules.name: The Reserved-Border Rule
rules.body: Selectable surfaces carry a 2px transparent border at rest so that showing the border on hover never moves anything.

dos: Do lead with Deep Harbour Navy for authority and Shallow Water Blue for anything actionable; let Sea Mist carry the page.
Do reach for weight before size when building hierarchy — 400 → 600 → 700 → 800 across a 14–20px range.
Do write layout in logical properties and reason right-to-left first.
Do give every new container 16px corners, 20px padding and the ambient rest shadow.
Do keep shadows navy-tinted (rgba(27,46,94,…)), diffuse and low-opacity.

Do define a colour once. The palette currently lives in three places — :root custom properties, Tailwind's untouched default theme, and const NAVY = "#1B2E5E" re-declared in six page files. New work consolidates toward :root; it does not add a seventh copy.
donts: Don't let the clinic half win. Grey-on-grey, borderless dense tables and compressed padding produce the cold medical-records screen this system explicitly rejects. Daylight and breathing room are load-bearing.
Don't use left or right in a style object unless the value is being selected from the language state.
Don't rely on shadcn variant classes (bg-primary, text-primary-foreground, border-ring, bg-background) until a token layer exists. They resolve to nothing today.
Don't introduce a warm or saturated hue as decoration. Green, amber and red mean success, caution and error — nothing else.
Don't use pure black or neutral grey for text or shadow anywhere.
Don't trust the .badge-* colour names; three of them are blue.
